What Zelda analyzed The work behind this report — counted, not estimated. 12 Pages analyzed 12 Sections searched 2 Categories analyzed Business Model & Growth Analysis Insufficient disclosed data to describe the business model. No revenue statement, no product statement, and no description of how ManyChat charges customers were found in the extracted evidence. The only operational data points are the company's self-reported traction figures — 140,000+ bots and 500M messages, contextualised on a 'Traction by Apr-16' slide [S1, S2] — which indicate usage activity but do not establish whether the model is subscription, usage-based, freemium, or otherwise. Who pays, at what price, and what drives expansion are not addressed in the extracted evidence. Information Readiness Score: 10/100 Present: • Stage indicator: Series A [P1] • Sector: Software [P2] • Traction metrics (self-reported, unverified, undated as-of): 140,000+ bots, 500M messages, contextualised as 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2] • Funding raised figure (narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt, unverified): $23.1M [C1, S3] Needs Validation: • All traction figures (no independent confirmation found) [C2, C3] • Funding raised figure (no external evidence found) [C1] • Revenue, burn rate, and unit economics (not found in extracted evidence) • Team composition and credentials (not found in extracted evidence) • Product description and value proposition (not found in extracted evidence) • Problem statement and target customer (not found in extracted evidence) • Market size and competitive landscape (not found in extracted evidence) • Business model and pricing (not found in extracted evidence) • Use of proceeds (not found in extracted evidence) Next evidence to supply: Audited or reviewed financial statements showing revenue, gross margin, and cash burn, accompanied by independent confirmation of the traction metrics. Supported Points Traction slide contextualised as 'Traction by Apr-16' reports 140,000+ bots created on the platform [S1] — a concrete scale indicator, though self-reported and unverified. The same traction slide reports 500M messages sent [S2], suggesting meaningful platform usage volume at the time of the slide, subject to the same self-reported caveat. Open Concerns The two primary traction figures — 140,000+ bots and 500M messages [S1, S2] — are self-reported, carry no precise as-of date (only the slide context 'Traction by Apr-16'), and were not independently verified [C2, C3]; it is unknown whether they reflect cumulative totals, active usage, or another measure. Pitch Deck Hunt lists $23.1M raised [C1, S3], but no external evidence confirmed this figure; the capital structure and investor roster are therefore unknown. No team information was found in the extracted evidence, making it impossible to assess whether the organisation has the capability to execute on its apparent growth trajectory. No revenue, pricing, or business model data was found in the extracted evidence, leaving open the question of whether the reported usage activity has translated into any commercial traction. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece is audited or independently reviewed financial statements — specifically revenue figures and gross margin — which would establish whether ManyChat's self-reported usage metrics [S1, S2] correspond to any monetisation and would allow the $23.1M funding figure (per Pitch Deck Hunt) [C1] to be contextualised against actual business performance.
